title: Natural full-workspace job overlap diagnostic
prompt:
Diagnostic only: determine whether a normal, substantial Rust workspace test job can remain running while you continue useful dependent development. Do not inspect or run the hidden verifier, private harness metadata, credentials, or host environment. Do not change README.md, contract.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, corpus files, public tests, or verifier. No network, sleeps, artificial delays, repeated no-op edits, or fake job IDs.

Use native CodeGG tools. Read the contract and the relevant Rust source/test files. Make one concrete contract-required Rust implementation change with a focused test in an unfinished crate. Then submit exactly one asynchronous `test` job with `cargo test --offline --locked --release --workspace`. Copy the exact returned `job_id` and immediately write `fixture/CONTINUATION.md` with that ID, the source change already made, and the next dependent phases.

Before the first `job status` call, make two separate, substantive dependent Rust source/test edits in later crates while that workspace test job runs. Do not query, wait, or submit another test between those edits. After both edits, call `job status` only with the exact returned job ID, up to five times until terminal. Report every observed status in order. If it reached terminal before the first status call, report that fact without resubmitting. If `running` is observed, make one more useful dependent source/test edit before the next exact-ID status call. Keep continuation current with the exact ID and observed states.

Stop after this one job reaches terminal or five exact-ID status calls. Summarize the observed states, whether a running state overlapped with the source edits, the exact edits made, and whether the test job completed. This is a scheduling/lifecycle diagnostic; do not claim H007 qualification and do not alter its acceptance criteria.
